title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Accelerator table** | A table mapping key combinations to command ids, translated in the message loop. (2.04) |
| **Anchor** | Which edges of its parent a control keeps a fixed distance from when the parent is resized. (3.03) |
| **BOM** | Byte order mark: bytes at the start of a text file that identify its encoding (`EF BB BF`, `FF FE`, `FE FF`). (6.01) |
| **Capture** | Directing all mouse messages to one window, even when the mouse is outside it. (2.02) |
| **Client area** | The inside of a window, without the frame, title bar and menu. (1.03) |
| **COM** | Windows' component object model: objects created by class id, used through interfaces, released when done. (3.02) |
| **Common controls** | List view, tree view, status bar and other controls from comctl32, drawn with visual styles in version 6. (3.05) |
| **Device context (HDC)** | A drawing surface with its current pen, brush, font and colours. (1.05) |
| **Device-dependent resource** | A Direct2D object on the GPU that must be re-created when the device is lost. (4.02) |
| **Dialog unit** | The layout unit of dialog templates, based on the dialog's font, so dialogs scale with text size. (3.01) |
| **DIP** | Device-independent pixel: 1/96 inch, Direct2D's unit when DPI is set. (4.02) |
| **Direct2D** | The GPU-accelerated 2D drawing API with antialiasing and transforms. (4.02) |
| **DirectWrite** | The text layout and rendering API used with Direct2D. (4.03) |
| **Double buffering** | Drawing a frame off-screen and copying it to the window in one step, to avoid flicker. (4.01) |
| **DPI awareness** | A program's declaration that it scales itself for the monitor's DPI instead of being stretched. (3.04) |
| **GDI** | The original Windows drawing API: device contexts, pens, brushes, fonts, bitmaps. (1.05) |
| **GetLastError** | Returns the thread's last error code, set by most failing API functions. (1.01) |
| **Handle** | An opaque value referring to a system object, closed with its type's own function. (1.01) |
| **HRESULT** | A 32-bit result code used by COM: negative means failure. (1.01) |
| **Invalid region** | The part of a window that needs repainting; WM_PAINT is sent while it is not empty. (1.05) |
| **Known folder** | A standard folder such as AppData or Documents, located with SHGetKnownFolderPath. (5.01) |
| **Manifest** | XML embedded in an .exe that sets visual styles, DPI awareness, privileges and more. (6.02) |
| **Message** | A notification (input, painting, timers, commands) delivered to a window procedure. (1.03) |
| **Message loop** | The loop that takes messages from the thread's queue and dispatches them. (1.03) |
| **Modal / modeless** | A dialog that blocks its owner until closed, or one that stays open alongside it. (3.01) |
| **Notification** | A control's message to its parent about an event: WM_COMMAND codes or WM_NOTIFY structures. (2.05, 3.05) |
| **Posted / sent message** | A message put in the queue and returned from at once, or delivered directly with the caller waiting. (1.04) |
| **Premultiplied alpha** | Pixels whose colour channels are already multiplied by their alpha. (4.04) |
| **Registry** | Windows' hierarchical database of keys and typed values. (5.02) |
| **Reparse point** | A junction or symbolic link in the file system, which can point anywhere, including back up the tree. (5.01) |
| **Resource** | Data compiled into the .exe: menus, dialogs, icons, strings, version information. (2.04) |
| **Share mode** | What other programs may do with a file while you have it open. (5.01) |
| **Surrogate pair** | Two UTF-16 code units encoding one code point above U+FFFF. (1.02) |
| **Text layout** | A DirectWrite object holding one string laid out in a box, for drawing and hit-testing. (4.03) |
| **UI thread** | The thread that owns the windows and runs the message loop; it must never block. (5.04) |
| **UTF-16** | The encoding Windows uses internally: 16-bit units, with surrogate pairs for rare characters. (1.02) |
| **Virtual list view** | A list view that stores no items and asks for the text of visible rows only. (3.05) |
| **Virtual-key code** | The number identifying a physical key in key messages, such as VK_LEFT or 'A'. (2.01) |
| **Visual styles** | The modern look of controls, enabled by the common controls version 6 manifest entry. (3.05) |
| **W and A functions** | The UTF-16 (wide) and legacy code page (ANSI) versions of text functions. (1.02) |
| **WIC** | The Windows Imaging Component, which decodes and encodes image files. (4.04) |
| **Window class** | A registered description of a kind of window, including its window procedure. (1.03) |
| **Window procedure** | The function that handles a window's messages. (1.03) |
| **Worker thread** | A thread that does slow work and posts results to the UI thread. (5.04) |
